author_or_org: Jason Ganz and Benoit Perigaud (dbt Labs)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A semantic layer is an ontology-driven approach that defines metrics, dimensions, entities, and their relationships to encode business logic; the LLM maps a question into metrics and dimensions, and MetricFlow deterministically generates SQL.
claims.quote: Instead of asking the LLM to write raw SQL, you define a structured ontology (metrics, dimensions, entities, and the relationships between them) that encodes your business logic. The LLM's job is then reduced to decomposing a natural language question into the correct combination of metrics and dimensions. dbt's Semantic Layer uses its engine MetricFlow to handle the actual query generation deterministically.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: For queries covered by a well-modeled Semantic Layer, accuracy approaches or hits 100% because deterministic query generation prevents subtly wrong results.
claims.quote: **For queries covered by a well-modeled Semantic Layer, accuracy approaches or hits 100%.** The Semantic Layer's deterministic query generation means the LLM can't produce subtly wrong results.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Text-to-SQL accuracy nearly doubled from 32.7% to 64.5% on the full benchmark question set.
claims.quote: **Text-to-SQL accuracy nearly doubled**, from 32.7% to 64.5% on the full question set. That's a massive improvement.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: For questions within the Semantic Layer's scope, both tested models returned correct results 100% of the time.
claims.quote: **For questions within the Semantic Layer's scope, both models now return correct results 100% of the time.**

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Semantic Layer failure is an error message when it cannot answer, whereas text-to-SQL failure can be a plausible but incorrect answer.
claims.quote: With text-to-SQL, failure looks like a plausible but incorrect answer. With the Semantic Layer, failure looks like an error message.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The Semantic Layer can only answer questions that fall within the scope of what has been modeled.
claims.quote: The trade-off is coverage: the Semantic Layer can only answer questions that fall within the scope of what's been modeled.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Adding just 3 additional models allowed the Semantic Layer to answer every benchmark question and also improved text-to-SQL.
claims.quote: With just 3 additional models, the Semantic Layer can now answer every question in the benchmark. And text-to-SQL improved too, confirming that **better modeling helps both approaches.**

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Text-to-SQL is flexible for any question if the data exists, but fragile because the LLM can join tables incorrectly, misinterpret a column, or return wrong results.
claims.quote: This makes it flexible (any question is fair game as long as the data exists), but also fragile. The LLM might join tables incorrectly, misinterpret a column's meaning, or produce a query that runs successfully but returns wrong results.
